comments.content: The content-size heuristic (inherited from `StaggeredGridScrollbarAdapter`) only looks at `visibleItemsInfo`. Unlike a staggered grid, a `LazyGrid` can contain full-span items — e.g. `AppsRoot` renders `ImportProposalBanner`/`KaoBanner` and section headers with `GridItemSpan(maxLineSpan)`, so their `column` is always 0. When the visible window happens to contain only such items, `laneCount` collapses to 1 and `avgHeight` becomes the banner/header height, making `rows = totalItemsCount` and `estimatedContentSize()` (and therefore `maxScrollOffset()`) too large by roughly the lane factor. The visible symptom is a tiny scrollbar thumb and drag positions that jump. Consider deriving the column count from a stable source (the grid's configured columns, or the last non-degenerate value) and averaging row height over a complete row of same-row items rather than over all visible items.

comments.content: `GridScrollbarAdapter.scrollOffset` re-runs `estimatedContentSize()` on every read, and that method allocates a fresh list via `visibleItems.map { it.size.height }.average()`. `scrollOffset` is polled by `VerticalScrollbar` during scroll/drag, so this produces per-frame garbage and O(n) work in a hot path. `visibleItems.sumOf { it.size.height } / visibleItems.size` avoids the intermediate list (and `scrollTo` can reuse a single `estimatedContentSize()` call instead of computing it via both `totalContent` and `maxScrollOffset`).

comments.content:
`gridColumnCount` only clamps the lower bound, so degenerate inputs are passed straight through to callers that feed `GridCells.Fixed(...)` / `StaggeredGridCells.Fixed(...)`:
- If `BoxWithConstraints` reports an unbounded width (e.g. inside a horizontally scrollable parent), `contentWidthDp` is `Float.POSITIVE_INFINITY` and `ceil(Infinity).toInt()` becomes `Int.MAX_VALUE`.
- If `maxCardWidthDp + spacingDp <= 0`, the divisor is zero/negative, producing `Infinity`/`NaN`.
Neither case is currently guarded or tested. Adding an `isFinite()`/positive-step guard makes the helper safe to reuse.
Minor related DRY point: the default `spacingDp = 10f` duplicates `CardGridSpec.GridSpacing = 10.dp` (and the `10.dp` literals in the callers), so the default can silently drift from the declared spec — referencing the spec removes the second source of truth.
comments.existing_code:
fun gridColumnCount(contentWidthDp: Float, maxCardWidthDp: Float, spacingDp: Float = 10f): Int =
    max(1, ceil((contentWidthDp - spacingDp) / (maxCardWidthDp + spacingDp)).toInt())
